clauses.current_legal_basis: The ordering lead of EO 11396 continues because the order states no end and the U.S. Code, eCFR and Office of the Federal Register disposition-note searches checked through 2026-10-14 found no instrument revoking or superseding the order.
clauses.reason: The ordering lead recites the President's authority under the Constitution and laws and directs the sections that follow; it states no end and no held later instrument ends it, so it remains in force on 2026-10-14 together with the sections it introduces.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The Attorney General's designation to facilitate and coordinate Federal law enforcement and crime prevention programs and to promulgate necessary rules, as set out in Section 1 of the held order, continues because no end is stated and the U.S. Code, eCFR and Office of the Federal Register disposition-note searches checked through 2026-10-14 found no instrument ending it.
clauses.reason: Section 1 designates the Attorney General to facilitate and coordinate the criminal law enforcement activities and crime prevention programs of all Federal departments and agencies and their assistance programs for State and local law enforcement, and lets the Attorney General promulgate rules and take actions necessary to carry out those functions. It states no duration or condition and no held later instrument amends, revokes or supersedes it. The recital of the Law Enforcement Assistance Act of 1965 is a whereas clause and is not the source of the command, which rests on the stated constitutional and statutory authority of the President. Section 1 therefore remains operative on 2026-10-14.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The direction in Section 2 of the held order that each department and agency cooperate with the Attorney General and furnish information on request continues because no end is stated and no instrument ending it was found in the searches checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: Section 2 directs each Federal department and agency to cooperate with the Attorney General and, to the extent permitted by law and within the limits of available funds, to furnish reports, information and assistance on request. It is a continuing direction with no stated end, and no held later instrument ends it, so it remains operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Read the held Federal Register text of EO 11396 (33 FR 2689, February 8, 1968; jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11396.txt) in full. The order's recitals are followed by two operative sections: Section 1 designates the Attorney General to facilitate and coordinate Federal criminal law enforcement and crime prevention programs and the departments' programs assisting State and local law enforcement, with authority to promulgate rules; Section 2 directs each department and agency to cooperate and furnish information. The dossier's prepared clause inventory points at a different document printed on the same pages, an Atomic Energy Commission amendment of 10 CFR Part 1, so the inventory is corrected by characters from the order's own text on PDF page 5. The order has no duration, expiry or condition. The three bounded machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes) show zero disposition notes; the U.S. Code and eCFR hits are leads only (the order is printed as a note to 34 U.S.C. chapter 101, and a held 2025 Department of Justice rule cites it as authority) and are not relied on as a legal basis. The held-corpus search for the order number finds only the order, the 1989 codification SOURCE line and that 2025 rule. The order is therefore operative on 2026-10-14 under the held original plus bounded search route. Limits: the U.S. Code search does not reflect laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14; the text is an OCR text layer of the official Federal Register page.
